sheet.capTabel: #  object{spatiu}orientation on the plate       colour to assign
sheet.grupMulticolor: ↳ {piese} = ONE SINGLE PIECE, printed multicolour — do not separate them
sheet.sec2: 2. COLOURS ARE ASSIGNED IN THE SLICER — A MANDATORY STEP
sheet.culoriIntro: The 3MF file carries the colour of every object, but slicers read it differently:
sheet.culoriPunct1: some ignore it entirely, others map it to slots other than the ones intended.
sheet.culoriPunct2: So the colour is NOT automatic. Assign it MANUALLY, object by object,
sheet.culoriPunct3: following the table in point 1. The HEX codes there are the reference.
sheet.culoriBambu: Bambu Studio / OrcaSlicer:  select the object in the list → right-hand panel →
sheet.culoriBambu2: “Filament” → pick the slot with the colour from the table.
sheet.culoriCura: Cura:                       select the object → pick the extruder in the top bar.
sheet.culoriVerif: Check in the preview that every object has the colour from the table BEFORE
sheet.culoriVerif2: starting the print. A wrong colour cannot be corrected after printing.
sheet.preaMulteCulori: ⚠ {n} distinct colours — more than the 4 AMS slots. This needs several
sheet.preaMulteCulori2: passes or manual filament changes. Plan them before you start.
sheet.print1: Do not rotate or flip the pieces: they are already oriented for printing, and
sheet.print2: the orientation in the table guarantees that the visible faces come out smooth.
sheet.print3: The positions on the plate are computed with a 5 mm margin and 3 mm between pieces.
sheet.print4: You may move them, but keep the pieces of the same group on the same plate.
sheet.montaj0: Clean the sockets of strings and support debris before assembling.
sheet.montajProba: Do a DRY fit, without glue: every piece must go in without being forced.
sheet.montajLipici: Recommended adhesive: cyanoacrylate in dots, not over the whole surface — the excess
sheet.montajLipici2: squeezes out at the edges and shows on the finished piece.
sheet.verif1: every piece goes into its socket, with no visible play
sheet.verif2: the colours match the table in point 1
sheet.verif3: the assembly stands steady, it does not rock
sheet.verif4: no adhesive marks are left on the visible faces

ajutor.subtitlu: Magic3D — what each tool does and how to use it
ajutor.sectiuneBara: THE TOOLS IN THE TOP BAR
ajutor.sectiuneCombinatii: HOW MANY DIFFERENT OBJECTS YOU CAN GET
ajutor.undo_d: Goes back to the state before the last change.
ajutor.undo_c: Ctrl+Z. Several steps are kept, so you can go back after a few mistakes too.
ajutor.redo_d: Re-applies the change you have just undone.
ajutor.move_d: Moves the selected object. The arrows show the directions it can actually move in.
ajutor.move_c: Drag an arrow for a single axis, or the square in the middle for free movement. Hold Shift for 1 mm steps. On the base, the letter slides horizontally; the lettering and the themes slide on the face of the letter, even when it is rotated.
ajutor.rotate_d: Rotates the selected object on one of the three axes.
ajutor.rotate_c: Drag a ring. Alt+drag directly on the object rotates it without grabbing a ring. The angle appears next to the cursor during the gesture.
ajutor.scale_d: Changes the size of a theme or of the base.
ajutor.scale_c: Drag a corner. In the panel you can turn off “keep the proportions” to scale on a single axis — useful for thickening an object that is too flat.
ajutor.depth_d: Sets how far the object sinks into the material of the letter.
ajutor.depth_c: Drag the handle or type the value in the panel. Negative = sinks in; the pocket is cut automatically, exactly as deep as the object is buried.
ajutor.align_d: Centres the selected object on the letter.
ajutor.align_c: You choose centring on X, on Y or on both. “Lay on the flat face” rotates an imported model so it rests with its largest face down.
ajutor.tematici_d: The library of decorative objects: balls, musical notes, playing cards and the rest.
ajutor.tematici_c: Click the tool, then the model. It is added onto the face of the letter, buried 3 mm, with the pocket cut automatically. Rescan if you have put new files in the folder.
ajutor.baza_d: The library of stands the letter is planted in.
ajutor.baza_c: You pick the base, then set its thickness and the embedding depth in the panel. The socket is cut to the outline of the sole, with a different depth for each foot.
ajutor.views_d: Jumps to a standard view: front, back, top, bottom, left, right, isometric.
ajutor.views_c: “Fit” brings the whole scene back into frame — useful after you get lost zooming.
ajutor.proj_c: Orthographic is better for checking alignment and dimensions, because it does not distort.
ajutor.plate_d: Choose the size of the printer plate.
ajutor.plate_c: It is used when arranging the pieces for export. Choose your printer's real plate.
ajutor.plates_d: Previews how the pieces are laid out on the plates.
ajutor.plates_c: If the pieces do not fit on one, they are split across several automatically, with a 5 mm margin and 3 mm between them.
ajutor.presets_d: Saves and reloads a complete configuration.
ajutor.presets_c: You save it under a name; the letter, font, lettering, themes, base, positions and colours are all kept. Useful for orders that repeat.
ajutor.imagine_d: Exports a PNG image of the model.
ajutor.imagine_c: You choose the width and the background, white or transparent. Transparent is good for catalogues and for compositing.
ajutor.prezentare_d: A mode for product photos: clean background, lights and scenes.
ajutor.prezentare_c: You pick the scene and the angle, then take the capture. The tools and the grid leave the frame.
ajutor.rigla_d: Measures the distance between two points on the model.
ajutor.rigla_c: A click on the model pins a point, the second click gives the distance. Points snap to corners if you are within 2 mm. You can rotate the piece between clicks — the tool stays open. The result appears in the middle of the line.
ajutor.setari_d: The company identity: logo, name, website — used for the watermark.
ajutor.setari_c: You load them once and they stay saved locally.
ajutor.export_d: Generates the files to print, plus the production sheet.
ajutor.export_c: The pieces are already oriented for printing. Next to the 3MF you get a .txt with the colour table, the assembly steps and the checklist. THE COLOURS ARE ASSIGNED IN THE SLICER, manually, following that table.
ajutor.flux1: 1. Choose the letter and the font. Set the height, the thickness and the border.
ajutor.flux2: 2. Write the text on the letter and choose the mode: relief, engraved or socket (inlay).
ajutor.flux3: 3. Add themes, if you want. Position them and set how far they sink into the material.
ajutor.flux4: 4. Add the base. Set its thickness, then how deep the letter is planted in it.
ajutor.flux5: 5. Check the status bar: contact with the base, floating objects, warnings.
ajutor.flux6: 6. Export. Open the 3MF in the slicer, assign the colours from the .txt sheet, print.
ajutor.flux7: 7. Clean the sockets, do a dry fit, then glue.
ajutor.sfat1: The status bar at the bottom is the most useful checking instrument: it shows the contact with the base, the objects without support, and everything that would ruin the print.
ajutor.sfat2: An object under 1 mm thick, buried 3 mm, disappears completely into the letter. Scale its thickness first.
ajutor.sfat3: If the letter touches the base on less than 40% of its sole, you get a warning: thicken the base and increase the embedding.
ajutor.sfat4: Changing the letter or the font is the slowest operation. The rest of the settings are almost instant.
ajutor.combIntro: Counting only the discrete choices, with one theme and one base:
ajutor.combFormula: {car} characters × {font} fonts × {mod} lettering modes × {baze} base variants × {tem} theme variants
ajutor.combNota1: The base and theme variants include the “none” option, which is why they are one more than the files in the library.
ajutor.combNota2: The number covers only the choices in the lists. The text you write, the dimensions, the colours, the positions and the rotations are continuous, so the real number of objects you can produce has no practical limit.

ornament.instrPlat:
Flat ornament

1. Print each ornament face up, without supports.
2. The base, text and rim are separate parts: give each its own filament (AMS) or change filament at the layer where the text starts.
3. Thread a ribbon or string through the hole.
ornament.instrGlobInel:
3D bauble

1. Print both halves on their cut face, dome up, without supports (the shell supports itself, the pole closes as a short bridge).
2. Print the joining ring lying flat.
3. Put the ring into the recess of one half, then press the other half over it.
4. If it is too tight, sand the ring lightly; if it is loose, a drop of glue.
ornament.instrGlobStifturi:
3D bauble

1. Print both halves on their cut face, dome up, without supports (the shell supports itself, the pole closes as a short bridge).
2. Cut 3 pieces of 1.75 mm filament, {lungime} mm each.
3. Put them into the holes of one half and press the other half over them.

stampila.avertSubtire: The design has lines thinner than {mm} mm ({mm2} mm² in total): they will not print or stamp cleanly. Thicken them, enlarge the stamp or pick a bolder font.
stampila.instrCerneala:
Ink stamp — two bodies:
1. The face (plate 1): TPU (95A), relief up, 0.12 mm layers, 100% infill.
2. The handle (plate 2): PLA, standing on its foot; the mark on top can be another colour.
3. Glue the face to the handle foot (TPU adhesive or gel superglue) with the small tabs on the rim lined up.
4. The design on the face is mirrored: it prints the right way round on paper, like the mark on top.
5. Use stamp ink; clean the face with soap and water.
stampila.instrLut:
Clay, fondant or cookie stamp — two bodies on one plate:
1. Print the face (relief up) and the handle in PLA; the face at 0.12 mm.
2. Glue the face to the handle foot with the small tabs on the rim lined up.
3. For food: use food-contact certified filament; FDM prints are porous, so wash right away and replace the stamp when it wears.
4. Dust the face with starch (fondant) or flour (dough) so it does not stick.
5. Press straight down, without twisting.

presa.avertFaraText: No text entered: the emblem comes out blank.
presa.avertFaraImagine: No picture uploaded: the emblem comes out without a design.
presa.avertNuIncape: The design does not fit in the emblem; enlarge it or shorten the text.
presa.avertFin: The emblem has details finer than {mm} mm ({mm2} mm² in total): paper will not take them. Thicken them or enlarge the emblem.
presa.instrCleste:
Clamp embosser — prints in one piece:
1. Print the arms open, as they lie on the plate, at 0.12 mm without supports: the hinge comes out assembled.
2. After printing, work the arms gently until the hinge frees up, then fold the arm with the recess over the one with the emblem.
3. The gap between the dies is {joc} mm (paper thickness + tolerance). Put the sheet between the dies, the side to be raised facing up, and squeeze the arms above the emblem.
4. For thicker card, raise “Paper thickness” and print again.
presa.instrPlaci:
Two-plate embosser:
1. Print the positive and the negative face up, at 0.12 mm.
2. Turn the negative over onto the positive: the pins go into the holes and line them up.
3. Put the sheet between the plates (the gap is {joc} mm), the side to be raised facing up, and press hard: by hand, in a vice or a desk press.

tava.instrTava:
Tray mold — open casting:
1. Print the tray face up without supports (the cavities have a draft angle).
2. Material: PETG for warm wax and hot-poured soap; PLA only for cold materials (plaster, resin, soap under 55 °C).
3. PLA and PETG are not food safe as printed (they are porous): for chocolate use food film or a food-grade resin coat, or use the tray as a master for food-grade silicone.
4. Coat the cavities with release agent (oil, petroleum jelly or spray) before pouring.
5. The piece, taken out and turned over, reads the right way: the cavity is the shape turned over, not mirrored.
tava.instrMaster:
Master for a silicone mold:
1. Print the master plate at 0.12 mm (the surface is copied into the silicone) and the frame on the second plate.
2. Set the frame on the plate around the plinth; seal the joint with plasticine or hot glue.
3. Coat the positives with release agent if the silicone needs it.
4. Mix the silicone (the volume is in the notes above) and pour it thin, from one corner, to avoid bubbles; {capac} mm stay above the tallest positive.
5. Once cured, remove the frame and peel the silicone. For food, use food-grade silicone.

presalut.textSus: Raised text on the top face
presalut.avertText: The text does not fit on the top face; shorten it or enlarge the press.
presalut.instrDoua:
Two-half press:
1. Print both halves cavity up, without supports.
2. Dust the cavities with starch (clay) or oil them lightly (soap).
3. Put a lump slightly larger than the piece in the bottom half, place the top half (the pins line it up; it closes one way only) and press: the excess escapes through the channel around.
4. Open, take the piece out and trim the flash from the edge.
5. For food: food-contact certified filament, washed right after use.

silicon.instructiuni:
Two-part silicone mold:
1. Print all parts. Glue the pour channel and the vents onto the positive at their marks (the highest points).
2. Set the walls in the groove of the base and hold them with the clips, slid down over the ribs; seal the joints with plasticine.
3. Put the parting plate on the base, inside the box, and the positive into its recess: the lower half of the model sits in the plate, the keys stick out on top.
4. First pour (top half): mix the silicone (the volume is in the notes above), degas it if you can and pour it thin, from one corner. Typical cure: 4–24 h depending on the silicone.
5. Turn the box over, remove the base and the parting plate (the positive stays in the silicone). Coat the cured silicone with release agent (petroleum jelly or silicone release spray) – otherwise the halves bond.
6. Second pour (bottom half), the same way; once cured, open the box, split the halves and take out the positive.
7. Times and mix ratios differ between silicones: check the data sheet of the one you use. For food, use food-grade silicone.
